title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
blurb: Introduced Group Relative Policy Optimization, which replaces PPO's value network with rewards normalised across a group of sampled answers, the RL algorithm behind later open reasoning models.
intro: For each question GRPO samples a group of answers, scores them, and uses each answer's reward relative to the group as its advantage, so no critic is trained. The loss keeps PPO's clipped ratio and adds a KL penalty to a reference model directly. The paper also compares outcome supervision, one reward per answer, with process supervision, a reward per reasoning step. The steps build group-relative advantages and their normalisation choices, KL estimators, the leave-one-out baseline and token aggregation; the capstone computes process-supervised advantages and the full loss.
